sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯·索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我在《纽约时报》的每日简报栏目 DealBook 负责商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市 DealBook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zilran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看到其中一些毫无防备、未经滤镜的对话实时发生。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch free at NYTimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 我们将在11月18日于 NYTimes.com 现场直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序来观看，并获得一个月的免费访问权限，畅读我们所有的报道。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 我希望你能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: For four minutes and 41 seconds last week, a little-known Republican official in Georgia came forward and said what dozens of national Republicans have so far been unwilling to say
sentences.zh: 上周，在长达4分41秒的时间里，佐治亚州一位鲜为人知的共和党官员站出来，说出了许多全国性共和党人迄今为止一直不愿说的话——

sentences.en: about the president's efforts to overturn the results of the election.
sentences.zh: 关于总统推翻选举结果的努力。

sentences.en: Today, a conversation with that official, Gabriel Sterling.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们将与这位官员加布里埃尔·斯特灵进行对话。

sentences.en: It's Monday, December 7th.
sentences.zh: 今天是12月7日，星期一。

sentences.en: Mr. Sterling?
sentences.zh: 斯特灵先生？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 在的。

sentences.en: Can you hear me?
sentences.zh: 你能听到我说话吗？

sentences.en: How are you, sir?
sentences.zh: 你好吗，先生？

sentences.en: I am running around like a one-armed paper hanger.
sentences.zh: 我忙得像个单臂挂壁纸的工人。

sentences.en: How about y'all?
sentences.zh: 你们怎么样？

sentences.en: I don't think I know that reference.
sentences.zh: 我想我不太懂这个比喻。

sentences.en: Well, think about it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，想想看。

sentences.en: If you're hanging wallpaper with one arm, it's very difficult.
sentences.zh: 如果你用一只胳膊挂壁纸，那是相当困难的。

sentences.en: Well, let's jump in.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们言归正传吧。

sentences.en: We really appreciate you making time for us, so thank you for doing this.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你抽出时间接受我们的采访，谢谢你这么做。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I want to start by asking you to describe your job and how that job fits into the Georgia election system.
sentences.zh: 我想先请你描述一下你的工作，以及这项工作是如何融入佐治亚州选举系统中的。

sentences.en: Well, it was sort of a new thing because after really 20 years, I guess 18 years, we replaced our old electronic-based voting system,
sentences.zh: 嗯，这算是一件新鲜事，因为在经历了实际上20年，我想是18年之后，我们更换了旧的基于电子的投票系统——

sentences.en: which was a no-paper system, where you'd go to a touchscreen, you'd cast your vote, and that touchscreen would hold the tabulation with a memory card.
sentences.zh: 那是一个无纸化系统，你会走到触摸屏前投票，然后该触摸屏会用存储卡保存计票结果。

sentences.en: But there was no paper trail.
sentences.zh: 但没有任何纸质记录。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: And as we saw moving forward after 2016, 2018, internally in the state of Georgia, it was decided we need to move to a paper-based system.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在2016年、2018年之后所看到的那样，在佐治亚州内部，人们决定我们需要转向基于纸质的系统。

sentences.en: And my job was really to kind of herd the cats of launching a system across 159 counties of a brand-new technology
sentences.zh: 而我的工作实际上就是要在159个县推行一项全新技术的系统，这就像赶猫上树一样——

sentences.en: with a lot more pieces and parts with a paper ballot component and get it all done.
sentences.zh: 里面有更多的零部件，包含纸质选票组件，并且要把这一切都完成。

sentences.en: And we were trying, we were struggling to find any project manager for this.
sentences.zh: 当时我们正在努力、在极力寻找这个项目的项目经理。

sentences.en: Every engineering firm, every company we went to, basically, we could have paid them a half a million dollars.
sentences.zh: 我们接触的每一家工程公司、每一家公司，基本上我们都可以付给他们五十万美元。

sentences.en: And they said, the lawyer's like, no, reputational risk is too high.
sentences.zh: 但他们的律师却说，不，声誉风险太高了。

sentences.en: I mean, we get one lawsuit, and we lose the money, and we lose the power of our brand.
sentences.zh: 我是说，只要吃上一场官司，我们就会赔钱，并且会失去品牌的影响力。

sentences.en: So we couldn't get anybody to do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我们找不到任何人来做这件事。

sentences.en: And finally, internally, I said, Gabe, you've been running this thing for essentially a year anyway.
sentences.zh: 最后在内部，我说，加布，反正你基本上已经运营这东西一年了。

sentences.en: You know all the ins and outs.
sentences.zh: 你对里里外外都门儿清。

sentences.en: It's too late to get somebody new.
sentences.zh: 现在找新人已经太晚了。

sentences.en: That's how I became the voting system implementation manager.
sentences.zh: 这就是我如何成为投票系统实施经理的经过。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And just to be clear about this new system and this new role that you were in, following issues with the voting process and claims of voter fraud in Georgia in 2016 and 2018,
sentences.zh: 为了弄清楚这个新系统以及你所处的新角色——在2016年和2018年佐治亚州出现投票过程问题和选举欺诈指控之后，

sentences.en: it was all intended to be building up to a secure and hopefully well-run 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 这一切本来都是为了建立一个安全且希望运作良好的2020年选举。

sentences.en: And your job, working from within Georgia's office of the Secretary of State, was essentially to be the guy that made sure everything was in place and that it all worked.
sentences.zh: 而你的工作，在佐治亚州州务卿办公室内部任职，基本上就是确保一切都准备就绪并正常运转的那个人。

sentences.en: Yes, that's essentially end of the day, boiling it down like good journalists do.
sentences.zh: 是的，归根结底就是这样，就像优秀的记者所做的那样，把事情简化了。

sentences.en: You got it.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I accept that praise.
sentences.zh: 我接受这个赞誉。

sentences.en: And Georgia's Secretary of State is a Republican.
sentences.zh: 佐治亚州的州务卿是一名共和党人。

sentences.en: Are you a Republican as well?
sentences.zh: 你也是共和党人吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lifelong.
sentences.zh: 老党员了。

sentences.en: And may I presume then that as a Republican, you are a supporter of the president?
sentences.zh: 那么我可以推测，作为一名共和党人，你也是总统的支持者吗？

sentences.en: You have voted for the president?
sentences.zh: 你投票给总统了吗？

sentences.en: I did vote for the president this time.
sentences.zh: 我这次确实投了总统的票。

sentences.en: I voted for him before.
sentences.zh: 我以前也投过他。

sentences.en: I mean, I hate talking about who I voted for.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我很讨厌谈论我投给了谁。

sentences.en: I'm a government functionary, but at this point in this role, you can't avoid that.
sentences.zh: 我是一个政府职员，但在目前的这个职位上，你无法避开这一点。

sentences.en: But yes, I did vote for him.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，我确实投了他。

sentences.en: So as a Republican and as someone who supports the president in general, I wonder how you felt when your state, this longtime Republican stronghold,
sentences.zh: 所以，作为一名共和党人，作为一个总体上支持总统的人，当你的州——这个长期的共和党大本营——

sentences.en: became so central to the outcome of this election and ultimately flipped blue for the first time since I think it was 1992.
sentences.zh: 变得对这次选举的结果如此关键，并最终自我记事起大概1992年以来首次翻蓝时，我想知道你是什么感受。

sentences.en: I knew – I've been around this for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我知道——我从事这行很久了。

sentences.en: I knew that it was – I mean, let's face it, in 2018, Stacey Abrams came within 55,000 votes of defeating Brian Kemp for governor.
sentences.zh: 我知道这是——咱们面对现实吧，在2018年，斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯差了不到55,000票就能击败布赖恩·坎普当选州长。

sentences.en: So we saw it coming.
sentences.zh: 所以我们早就预料到了。

sentences.en: And the people who were so shocked by this are people who haven't watched Georgia.
sentences.zh: 而那些对此感到无比震惊的人，都是没有关注佐治亚州局势的人。

sentences.en: Two of our big suburban counties, Cobb and Gwinnett, that had been Republican forever, flipped to, you know, Democrat control.
sentences.zh: 我们两个最大的郊区县，科布县和格威内特县，以前永远是共和党的地盘，结果翻盘落入了民主党的掌控。

sentences.en: And, you know, they went for Stacey Abrams in 2018.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，他们在2018年支持了斯泰西·艾布拉姆斯。

sentences.en: There was nothing you saw in the progression of votes that jumped out.
sentences.zh: 你在选票的发展过程中看不到任何突兀的东西。

sentences.en: I was like, wow, that's really anomalous.
sentences.zh: 我当时不会觉得，哇，这太异常了。

sentences.en: That's really strange if you're paying attention to what's on the ground.
sentences.zh: 如果你关注实地情况，就会觉得这其实并不奇怪。

sentences.en: And it was about Wednesday evening, I guess, when I was kind of looking at what was out still and kind of looking at what was still coming in,
sentences.zh: 大概是在周三晚上，我想，当时我正在查看还有哪些票没统计完，以及预计还有多少票会进来，

sentences.en: knowing the counties and the volume of votes that were there.
sentences.zh: 了解各县的情况以及那里的选票数量。

sentences.en: I started talking internally.
sentences.zh: 我开始在内部进行讨论。

sentences.en: I said, okay, we've got to prepare for this because it looks like the president's going to lose by about 10,000.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我们得为此做好准备，因为看起来总统要以大约1万票的劣势落败了。

sentences.en: And I was spitballing at that point.
sentences.zh: 我当时只是在凭直觉粗略估计。

sentences.en: I was pretty darn close.
sentences.zh: 结果我猜得相当准。

sentences.en: So we started knowing it was going to happen because, you know, Tuesday into Wednesday, let's set the stage a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始知道这会发生，因为，你知道，从周二到周三，让我们稍微还原一下当时的场景。

sentences.en: In June, we had a very successful election with the exception of really one county, which is our largest county, Fulton.
sentences.zh: 在6月份，我们举行了一场非常成功的选举，除了一个县——也就是我们最大的县，富尔顿县——之外。

sentences.en: And they had about 70% of our issues.
sentences.zh: 他们集中了我们大约70%的问题。

sentences.en: They had lines.
sentences.zh: 他们排起了长队。

sentences.en: They had technical issues.
sentences.zh: 他们遇到了技术问题。

sentences.en: They weren't really technical issues.
sentences.zh: 其实那并不是什么技术问题。

sentences.en: They were training issues.
sentences.zh: 那是培训问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, they had – the lines come from that.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，排长队就是由此产生的。

sentences.en: So we were really hyper-focused on having a successful election in November.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真正高度聚焦于在11月份举行一场成功的选举。

sentences.en: And Secretary Raffensperger had launched his November plan of action, which was we were going to have a tech in every single precinct.
sentences.zh: 拉芬斯珀格书记推出了他的11月行动计划，也就是我们要在每一个投票站都配备一名技术人员。

sentences.en: We were going to have the three weeks of early voting plus a mandate this Saturday and no excuse absentee.
sentences.zh: 我们要进行为期三周的提前投票，再加上周六强制投票以及无理由缺席投票。

sentences.en: We built an absentee ballot portal to make it easier for people to request them and easier for them to process them.
sentences.zh: 我们建立了一个缺席选票门户网站，以便人们更容易申请缺席投票，也更便于我们处理。

sentences.en: We had 1.3 million votes in on absentee by mail.
sentences.zh: 我们通过邮寄缺席投票收到了130万张选票。

sentences.en: We had 2.4 million, I think, in on early voting.
sentences.zh: 我想，通过提前投票收到了240万张。

sentences.en: And we had about 990,000 in on election day.
sentences.zh: 我们在选举日当天收到了大约99万张。

sentences.en: So we had no lines.
sentences.zh: 所以我们没有排长队。

sentences.en: The average wait in Georgia on November 3rd was three minutes.
sentences.zh: 11月3日，佐治亚州的平均等待时间是三分钟。

sentences.en: Three.
sentences.zh: 三分钟。

sentences.en: So pretty smooth.
sentences.zh: 所以相当顺利。

sentences.en: We were in victory lap mode, man.
sentences.zh: 我们当时简直进入了庆祝胜利的模式，老兄。

sentences.en: We had slayed the dragon of long lines.
sentences.zh: 我们斩断了排长队这条恶龙。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: You said victory lap mode, which is interesting to hear and I guess kind of speaks to your priorities.
sentences.zh: 你用了“庆祝胜利模式”这个词，听到这个很有意思，我想这也某种程度上说明了你的首要任务是什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because your preferred presidential candidate lost, but you're saying the election felt like a victory nevertheless because the election went smoothly.
sentences.zh: 因为你支持的总统候选人落败了，但你却说选举依然感觉像是一场胜利，因为选举进行得很顺利。

sentences.en: Our job is to run a good, safe, secure election.
sentences.zh: 我们的工作就是举办一场良好、安全、有保障的选举。

sentences.en: Every human being has their own preferences.
sentences.zh: 每个人都有自己的喜好。

sentences.en: But if you're a professional, you ignore all that and just do the job.
sentences.zh: 但如果你是一个专业人士，你就会把这些统统抛开，只管做好工作。

sentences.en: And in this role, we're working with the safety and security of the election system so people have faith in the outcome.
sentences.zh: 在这个岗位上，我们致力于维护选举系统的安全与保障，这样人们才会对结果充满信心。

sentences.en: And if you do anything that could undermine that, that's negative for the republic.
sentences.zh: 如果你做了任何可能破坏这一点的事情，这对共和国来说就是不利的。

sentences.en: And that's our main goal is to protect that.
sentences.zh: 而我们主要的宏伟目标就是保护这一点。

sentences.en: So in the end, as you've hinted at, this is a very close race, so close it ends up triggering a recount in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 所以最后，正如你所暗示的，这是一场非常胶着的竞赛，胶着到最终在佐治亚州引发了重新计票。

sentences.en: So what did you think when the president began to challenge the results of this very smooth election?
sentences.zh: 那么，当总统开始对这场如此顺利的选举结果提出质疑时，你是怎么想的？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I thought, okay, this is America.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我想，好吧，这里是美国。

sentences.en: We have due process.
sentences.zh: 我们有正当程序。

sentences.en: And there's always going to be illegal votes.
sentences.zh: 总会有违规选票的。

sentences.en: There's always going to be things because it happens in every single election.
sentences.zh: 总会有各种状况发生，因为每一场选举都会这样。

sentences.en: You know why?
sentences.zh: 你知道为什么吗？

sentences.en: It involves human beings.
sentences.zh: 因为它涉及人类。

sentences.en: The most flawed part of the system is always going to be human beings.
sentences.zh: 系统中最有缺陷的部分永远是人类。

sentences.en: Between the voters, the elections workers, the poll workers, people will make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 无论是选民、选举工作人员、投票站工作人员，人们都会犯错。

sentences.en: I mean, we know there's going to be a handful of dead people who vote.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我们知道总会有少数已故的人投票。

sentences.en: We know there's going to be a handful of people who double vote.
sentences.zh: 我们知道总会有少数人重复投票。

sentences.en: We do everything we can to put up roadblocks and try to catch that on the front end.
sentences.zh: 我们竭尽全力设置路障，试图在前端拦截这些情况。

sentences.en: But there's nothing looking like 13,000 or some grand conspiracy.
sentences.zh: 但没有任何迹象表明有1.3万张违规票或者存在什么宏大的阴谋。

sentences.en: And then, and it was really funny.
sentences.zh: 然后，这就很有趣了。

sentences.en: If you go back and look at the timeline, it didn't flip fully.
sentences.zh: 如果你回头看看时间线，它并没有完全翻转。

sentences.en: And we didn't finish everything off until really about eight or nine days out from the election.
sentences.zh: 直到选举结束后大约八到九天，我们才真正完成了所有工作。

sentences.en: And neither side knew what to say because if they started attacking the system, they might still win and they look foolish.
sentences.zh: 双方都不知道该说什么，因为如果他们开始攻击这个系统，他们可能最终还是会赢，那样看起来就很愚蠢了。

sentences.en: They'd be attacking their victory, right?
sentences.zh: 那不就变成在攻击他们自己的胜利了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: So they, so everybody kind of froze for a minute.
sentences.zh: 所以他们——每个人都僵住了一会儿。

sentences.en: And then when it was obvious that, that the president had come in second, that's when it seemed to sort of flip.
sentences.zh: 然后，当总统显然获得第二名时，局势似乎就发生了某种反转。

sentences.en: But at that point, you'd already had sort of the Michigan conspiracy theories out there in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 但在那个时候，密歇根州和宾夕法尼亚州的那些阴谋论已经满天飞了。

sentences.en: And they kind of built on those because we use Dominion voting systems here in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 他们顺着那些阴谋论继续发挥，因为我们在佐治亚州使用的是多米星投票系统（Dominion voting systems）。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, Dominion is the name of the contractor that you work with.
sentences.zh: 顺便说明一下，Dominion（多米星）就是与你们合作的承包商的名字。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But if you look at Dominion, a simple look at math will show you that they couldn't have been part of some grand Venezuelan ghost conspiracy from Hugo Chavez.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看 Dominion，只要稍微算一下数学就会发现，他们根本不可能参与乌戈·查韦斯那样的宏大委内瑞拉幽灵阴谋。

sentences.en: I mean, in the counties in Wisconsin where Dominion was used, President Trump won 59% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 我是说，在威斯康星州使用 Dominion 的那些县里，特朗普总统赢得了59%的选票。

sentences.en: In the counties in Pennsylvania where Dominion voting systems were used, he got 52.5% of the vote.
sentences.zh: 在宾夕法尼亚州使用 Dominion 投票系统的那些县里，他获得了52.5%的选票。

sentences.en: And did they have such a crazy algorithm that in Georgia, he won the places he was supposed to win.
sentences.zh: 难道他们拥有如此疯狂的算法，以至于在佐治亚州，他赢了他该赢的地方？

sentences.en: He lost the place he was supposed to lose, but lost it by just enough while the Republicans won other things, you know, to make it.
sentences.zh: 他输了他该输的地方，但输得恰到好处，而共和党人赢得了其他一些选举，你知道，好让这一切发生？

sentences.en: It's just, it's fever dream level of crazy if you want to, unless you want to ignore math.
sentences.zh: 这简直是发烧友梦呓般的疯狂，除非你想故意无视数学。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that math doesn't add up.
sentences.zh: 而这些数学根本对不上号。

sentences.en: Math doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 数学根本行不通。

sentences.en: I mean, that's what's so frustrating about a lot of these conspiracy theories is this simple, quick, critical thinking would show you this is crap.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这些阴谋论最让人沮丧的地方就在于，只要进行简单、快速的批判性思考，就会发现这全都是狗屁。

sentences.en: This is nothing.
sentences.zh: 这根本子虚乌有。

sentences.en: So do I have it right in saying that at first you watched what the president was doing and you respected his right to question the results?
sentences.zh: 所以我这样理解对吗：起初你看着总统的所作所为，你尊重他质疑结果的权利？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But as time went on and his claims and the claims of those around him felt increasingly kind of untethered from reality, you became more and more frustrated.
sentences.zh: 但随着时间的推移，他的主张以及他身边之人的主张越来越让人觉得脱离现实，你变得越来越沮丧。

sentences.en: Yes, especially early on what happened is threats started coming in to Secretary Raffensperger's wife of 40 years, Tricia, like on her cell phone, like sexualized violent threats.
sentences.zh: 是的，特别是刚开始的时候，威胁开始涌向拉芬斯珀格（Raffensperger）秘书结婚40年的妻子崔茜（Tricia），比如发到她的手机上，是一些带有性暗示的暴力威胁。

sentences.en: And that began the process where we got him Georgia State Patrol protection.
sentences.zh: 这就开启了我们为他安排佐治亚州州警（Georgia State Patrol）保护的进程。

sentences.en: And then I started doing the briefing.
sentences.zh: 然后我开始做简报。

sentences.en: So I was on television way more than somebody with the title of voting system implementation manager ought to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我在电视上露面的次数，远比一个顶着投票系统实施经理头衔的人应该露面的次数要多得多。

sentences.en: So you're literally going out to a podium and starting to brief people on what you know about the count and questions.
sentences.zh: 所以你实际上是要走到讲台前，开始向人们简要介绍你所了解的计票情况和各种问题。

sentences.en: We were doing two press conferences a day and doing hourly press releases.
sentences.zh: 我们一天开两次新闻发布会，每小时发布一次新闻稿。

sentences.en: We were as transparent as we could possibly be about what was going on, where were the votes, where was the process, you know, everything.
sentences.zh: 对于正在发生的事情、选票在哪里、流程进行到哪一步，你知道的，所有这一切，我们都尽可能地做到公开透明。

sentences.en: So I started getting some threats too.
sentences.zh: 所以我开始收到一些威胁。

sentences.en: And when you say you start getting threats, and I don't want to be too graphic here or gratuitous about this, but what do you mean?
sentences.zh: 当你说你开始受到威胁时，我不想在这里说得太生动或是不必要地直白，但你指的是什么？

sentences.en: Okay, like the simple one that has kind of stuck with me was, you know, I turned 50 on November 14th.
sentences.zh: 好吧，比如说那个一直留在脑海里的简单例子，你知道的，我在11月14日过了50岁生日。

sentences.en: So somebody tweeted up, enjoy your last birthday cake.
sentences.zh: 于是有人在推特上发文说，好好享用你最后一个生日蛋糕吧。

sentences.en: You know, those kind of things.
sentences.zh: 你知道，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: But then my cell phone number is out there publicly.
sentences.zh: 但后来我的手机号码在网上公开了。

sentences.en: I used to be a public elected official.
sentences.zh: 我曾经是一名公众选出的官员。

sentences.en: I was on the city council in Sandy Springs.
sentences.zh: 我曾是桑迪斯普林斯（Sandy Springs）的市议员。

sentences.en: So it's sort of out there in the internet world.
sentences.zh: 所以它差不多就存在于互联网世界里。

sentences.en: So I started getting text messages.
sentences.zh: 于是我开始收到短信。

sentences.en: And so I talked to the state patrol guys here, and I talked to my local police chief, which was helpful for being on the city council formally.
sentences.zh: 我和这里的州警聊过，也和当地的警察局长聊过，这对于我曾正式担任市议员很有帮助。

sentences.en: I knew him personally.
sentences.zh: 我个人认识他。

sentences.en: So I've had police protection around me.
sentences.zh: 所以我周围一直有警察保护。

sentences.en: And so that's sort of when it started getting to be a little nutball crazy town around us, you know.
sentences.zh: 所以，从某种程度上讲，周围的情况就是从那时开始变得有点像疯人院一样的疯狂，你知道的。

sentences.en: So we started watching it continue to sort of amp up.
sentences.zh: 于是我们开始看着这种情况继续升级。

sentences.en: And then, if we're going to get to that point, I guess that Tuesday where I had, for what people down here are referring to as the moment, about an hour,
sentences.zh: 然后，如果我们打算说到那个点，我想就是那个星期二，我有了被这里的人称为“那个时刻”的经历，在大约一个小时、

sentences.en: hour and a half before that, I got a call from the project manager from Dominion Voting Systems from over in Colorado.
sentences.zh: 在一个半小时之前，我接到了来自科罗拉多的多米尼恩投票系统（Dominion Voting Systems）项目经理的电话。

sentences.en: And she was audibly shaken.
sentences.zh: 而且她的声音明显在颤抖。

sentences.en: I had heard something about some videos going around.
sentences.zh: 我听说了一些关于流传视频的事情。

sentences.en: And, you know, we have people doing videos and claiming things.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们有人在拍视频并声称各种事情。

sentences.en: We have people stalking our warehouses and videoing everything going on, saying, you're going to prison to folks.
sentences.zh: 我们有人在仓库外盯梢，把发生的一切都拍下来，对大家说，你们要进监狱了。

sentences.en: You have people with video cameras stalking your warehouses, meaning the places where voting is being counted.
sentences.zh: 你们有人拿着摄像机在仓库外盯梢，也就是清点选票的地方。

sentences.en: Or not voting necessarily, just like our Center for Elections warehouse.
sentences.zh: 或者倒也不一定是投票，只是像我们的选举中心仓库。

sentences.en: There's really nothing there except for our election management system.
sentences.zh: 那里真的什么也没有，只有我们的选举管理系统。

sentences.en: And here we had a warehouse guy.
sentences.zh: 这里我们有一个仓库工作人员。

sentences.en: He's a warehouse guy.
sentences.zh: 他是个仓库员工。

sentences.en: He's putting stuff outside in the trash and loading things up.
sentences.zh: 他把东西拿到外面扔进垃圾桶，还在装载物品。

sentences.en: Like, you're going to prison.
sentences.zh: 就像是，你们要进监狱了。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Things like that.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: So we had the police go out and try to get people back from that.
sentences.zh: 于是我们派警察去试图把人们从那里驱散开。

sentences.en: And so that Tuesday, when I got the call from the project manager from Dominion Voting Systems, and I heard about this video,
sentences.zh: 所以在那个星期二，当我接到多米尼恩投票系统项目经理的电话，并听说这段视频时，

sentences.en: so I went and finally looked up the tweets and everything going around it.
sentences.zh: 于是我跑去最终查阅了推特以及所有与之相关的言论。

sentences.en: And there was a kid, and I finally talked to him and found out what it was.
sentences.zh: 有个年轻人，我最后跟他交谈过，并弄清楚了是怎么回事。

sentences.en: On the election management system, he was taking something called a batch report, which is one of the steps you do in a recount to make sure we're scanning this many batches.
sentences.zh: 在选举管理系统上，他当时正在拿一样叫批次报告的东西，这是重新计票时要做的步骤之一，用来确保我们扫描了这么多批次。

sentences.en: This is how many ballots are in this batch.
sentences.zh: 这一批里有多少张选票。

sentences.en: It's a check to make sure you're catching everything and you're tracking it properly.
sentences.zh: 这是一个核对步骤，用来确保你没有漏掉任何东西并进行了正确追踪。

sentences.en: So you take that report off, and he took it to a county computer to put it in so he could put it in an Excel spreadsheet, read it, and print it so they could check everything off.
sentences.zh: 所以你把那份报告拿下来，他把它拿到一台县里的电脑上输入进去，这样他就可以把它放进Excel电子表格里、读取并打印出来，以便他们核对所有内容。

sentences.en: Pretty standard.
sentences.zh: 挺标准的。

sentences.en: Yeah, very standard.
sentences.zh: 是的，非常标准。

sentences.en: So the guy comes in, and these two guys are watching it, and they're these QAnon conspiracy folks.
sentences.zh: 然后那家伙进来了，这两个人在看着，他们是那种匿名者Q（QAnon）阴谋论分子。

sentences.en: And it's like, look at this guy.
sentences.zh: 他们就像是，看看这家伙。

sentences.en: And they call him Nerd Boy.
sentences.zh: 他们叫他书呆子男孩（Nerd Boy）。

sentences.en: He's like moving stuff around.
sentences.zh: 他好像在搬弄东西。

sentences.en: He's manipulating votes.
sentences.zh: 他在篡改选票。

sentences.en: We're watching him.
sentences.zh: 我们在看着他。

sentences.en: He's stealing the election right here.
sentences.zh: 他就在这里窃取选举。

sentences.en: He's committing treason.
sentences.zh: 他在叛国。

sentences.en: So they put that out.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把这个发了出去。

sentences.en: It goes on to those QAnon kind of message boards and whatever place those go.
sentences.zh: 它被发到了那些匿名者Q类的留言板上，以及这类东西传播的任何地方。

sentences.en: So people figure out who this pretty anonymous-sounding young contractor is from Dominion, and they put his name out there.
sentences.zh: 于是人们查出了这个听起来相当匿名的多米尼恩年轻合同工是谁，并把他的名字公布了出去。

sentences.en: And they get his name, and it's a very unique name.
sentences.zh: 他们弄到了他的名字，那是一个非常独特的名字。

sentences.en: So not only is he catching flack, his family members are catching flack.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅他遭到猛烈抨击，他的家人们也遭到了抨击。

sentences.en: And the one I finally just snapped was I was scrolling through the Twitter thing, and there was this guy put up there.
sentences.zh: 而最终让我彻底爆发的那次，是我在刷推特动态时，看到有家伙发了这么一条。

sentences.en: They said the kid's name.
sentences.zh: 他们说出了那孩子的名字。

sentences.en: I say kid.
sentences.zh: 我说孩子。

sentences.en: He's a 20-something.
sentences.zh: 他二十多岁。

sentences.en: He's a guy who took a job.
sentences.zh: 他只是个接了一份工作的人。

sentences.en: He's a contractor.
sentences.zh: 他是个合同工。

sentences.en: He's an IT guy and had his name.
sentences.zh: 他是个IT人员，上面有他的名字。

sentences.en: He goes, you've committed treason.
sentences.zh: 他写道，你犯下了叛国罪。

sentences.en: May God have mercy on your soul with a swinging noose and a gif.
sentences.zh: 愿上帝怜悯你的灵魂，还配了一个摇晃的绞索动图。

sentences.en: And at that point, I was done.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，我忍无可忍了。

sentences.en: I said, this is it.
sentences.zh: 我说，够了。

sentences.en: And I went to the Deputy Secretary, Jordan Fuchs, and Secretary Brad Raffensperger and said, I think we've got to say something.
sentences.zh: 我去找了副秘书长乔丹·富克斯（Jordan Fuchs）和秘书布拉德·拉芬斯珀格（Brad Raffensperger），说，我觉得我们必须说点什么了。

sentences.en: And they could tell I was pissed.
sentences.zh: 他们能看出我气炸了。

sentences.en: So let's talk about this moment.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈这个时刻。

sentences.en: You go to your boss, you go to Secretary Raffensperger, and you say, I think I need to do something.
sentences.zh: 你去找你的老板，去找拉芬斯珀格秘书，然后你说，我觉得我需要做点什么。

sentences.en: What happened?
sentences.zh: 发生了什么？

sentences.en: Set the scene for me.
sentences.zh: 给我还原一下当时的场景。

sentences.en: Well, I went to Jordan, the Deputy Secretary, firSt.
sentences.zh: 好的，我先去找了副秘书长乔丹。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And I kind of walked her through it, and I was like, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 我跟她大致过了一遍情况，当时我就说，我受够了。

sentences.en: We got to say, she's like, okay.
sentences.zh: 我们必须表态，她说，好吧。

sentences.en: They didn't tell me what to say, but she got the Secretary on the phone and said, listen, Gabe wants to go do this.
sentences.zh: 他们没有告诉我该说什么，但她把秘书叫到了电话上，并说，听着，盖布（Gabe）想去把这事做了。

sentences.en: And I believe his exact words, let him go do what he does.
sentences.zh: 我记得他的原话大致是，让他去做他该做的事吧。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: What did you interpret that to mean?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: Let me go do what I do, which meant at that point, they knew how pissed I was, and they said, you just go say what needs to be said.
sentences.zh: 让我去做我该做的事，这意味着在那时，他们知道我有多生气，他们说，你就去说该说的话吧。

sentences.en: I didn't get marching orders, but you saw the next day, he said, I agree with him.
sentences.zh: 我没有接到具体指令，但你看第二天，他说，我同意他的看法。

sentences.en: I wouldn't have necessarily used the exact words because he's a much more soft-spoken man than I am.
sentences.zh: 我未必会用完全相同的词句，因为他比我要温和得多。

sentences.en: But he said, go do it.
sentences.zh: 但他说，去干吧。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So what's next?
sentences.zh: 接下来是什么？

sentences.en: Well, we already had a previously scheduled conference because, like I said, we've been doing commonly two-a-days.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们之前已经计划好了一场发布会，因为就像我说的，我们通常一天开两次。

sentences.en: News conference, yep.
sentences.zh: 新闻发布会，没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we had been, you know, we were in the middle of the recount at this point, kind of explaining the process and where we were and everything.
sentences.zh: 而且我们一直在，你知道的，当时我们正处于重新计票的中间阶段，要解释整个流程以及我们所处的位置等等。

sentences.en: So I knew I had about an hour, which was probably good for me because I kind of calmed down a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道我还有一个小时左右的时间，这对我可能挺好的，因为我情绪稍微冷静了一些。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But I don't write things down.
sentences.zh: 但我不会把稿子写下来。

sentences.en: I'm not scripted.
sentences.zh: 我不是按稿宣读的。

sentences.en: I just kind of riff.
sentences.zh: 我只是即兴发挥。

sentences.en: So I knew it was coming, and I was coming down some.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道这件事要来，而且我的情绪也平复了一些。

sentences.en: And I had some ideas of the direction I was going to go, but I never know exactly what I'm going to say.
sentences.zh: 我大致有一些要讲的方向，但我永远不知道自己具体会说些什么。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I remember walking out of the door, and I still had to do the regular briefing, but I walked up.
sentences.zh: 我记得我走出门时，依然得做常规的简报，但我走了过去。

sentences.en: Okay, this is going to be kind of a two-parter, guys.
sentences.zh: 好了，伙计们，这大概会分为两个部分。

sentences.en: It's going to feel.
sentences.zh: 感觉会是这样。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: But this is going to be a little different.
sentences.zh: 但这会有所不同。

sentences.en: And that's why I said it's kind of put my hands on the podium.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我说，我把双手按在了讲台上。

sentences.en: And I had no idea what I was going to say, but it just flowed.
sentences.zh: 我根本不知道自己要说些什么，但它就是自然地流露出来了。

sentences.en: Good afternoon.
sentences.zh: 下午好。

sentences.en: My name is Gabriel Sterling.
sentences.zh: 我叫加布里埃尔·斯特林（Gabriel Sterling）。

sentences.en: I'm the Boating System Implementation Manager for the state of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我是佐治亚州的投票系统实施经理。

sentences.en: And just to give you all a heads up, this is going to be sort of a two-part press conference today.
sentences.zh: 为了让大家心里有个底，今天的新闻发布会将分为两个部分。

sentences.en: At the beginning of this, I'm going to do my best to keep it together because it has all gone too far.
sentences.zh: 在开始的时候，我会尽力控制住自己的情绪，因为这一切都已经太过分了。

sentences.en: All of it.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切。

sentences.en: I didn't know I was going to call out the president until about 20 seconds in.
sentences.zh: 直到大约20秒钟前，我才知道我要点名总统。

sentences.en: So at that point, I kind of made the decision.
sentences.zh: 所以在那个时候，我算是做了这个决定。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: And I finally, like I said, it just, it was in my gut, and it all just kind of went.
sentences.zh: 最后，就像我说的，这就，这是我发自内心的直觉，然后一切就这么倾泻而出了。

sentences.en: So.
sentences.zh: 所以。

sentences.en: It has to stop.
sentences.zh: 必须停止了。

sentences.en: Mr. President, you have not condemned these actions or this language.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，您还没有谴责这些行为或这种言论。

sentences.en: Senators, you have not condemned this language or these actions.
sentences.zh: 参议员们，你们还没有谴责这种言论或这些行为。

sentences.en: This has to stop.
sentences.zh: 这必须停止了。

sentences.en: We need you to step up, and if you're going to take a position of leadership, show some.
sentences.zh: 我们需要你们挺身而出，既然你们要占据领导地位，就展现出一点领导力来。

sentences.en: My boss, Secretary Raffensperger, his address is out there.
sentences.zh: 我的老板，拉芬斯珀格秘书，他的住址被曝光了。

sentences.en: They've had people doing caravans in front of their house.
sentences.zh: 有人开车在他们家门前游行抗议。

sentences.en: They've had people come onto their property.
sentences.zh: 有人闯入了他们的私人领地。

sentences.en: Trisha, his wife of 40 years, is getting sexualized threats through her cell phone.
sentences.zh: 崔茜，他结婚40年的妻子，正通过手机受到带有性暗示的威胁。

sentences.en: It has to stop.
sentences.zh: 这必须停止了。

sentences.en: This is elections.
sentences.zh: 这是选举。

sentences.en: This is the backbone of democracy, and all of you who have not said a damn word are complicit in this.
sentences.zh: 这是民主的基石，而你们所有连一句该死的话都没说的人，都是这里的帮凶。

sentences.en: It's too much.
sentences.zh: 这实在太过了。

sentences.en: Yes, fight for every legal vote.
sentences.zh: 是的，为每一张合法的选票而战。

sentences.en: Go through your due process.
sentences.zh: 走完你们的正当法律程序。

sentences.en: We encourage you, use your First Amendment.
sentences.zh: 我们鼓励你们，行使你们的宪法第一修正案权利。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 这没问题。

sentences.en: Death threats.
sentences.zh: 死亡威胁。

sentences.en: Physical threats.
sentences.zh: 人身威胁。

sentences.en: Intimidation.
sentences.zh: 恐吓。

sentences.en: It's too much.
sentences.zh: 这太过分了。

sentences.en: It's not right.
sentences.zh: 这不对。

sentences.en: They've lost the moral high ground to claim that it is.
sentences.zh: 他们已经失去了宣称这没问题的道义制高点。

sentences.en: I don't have all the best words to do this because I'm angry.
sentences.zh: 我没有最华丽的词藻来表达这一切，因为我很愤怒。

sentences.en: And the straw that broke the camel's back today is, again, this 20-year-old contractor for a voting system company just trying to do his job.
sentences.zh: 而今天压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草，依然是这位投票系统公司的20岁年轻合同工，他只是在努力做好他的工作。

sentences.en: Just there.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是因为他在那儿。

sentences.en: In fact, I talked to Dominion today and I said he's one of the better ones they got.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我今天和多米尼恩谈过，我说他是他们那儿表现较好的员工之一。

sentences.en: His family's getting harassed now.
sentences.zh: 而他的家人现在却受到了骚扰。

sentences.en: There's a noose out there with his name on it.
sentences.zh: 外面甚至挂着写有他名字的绞索。

sentences.en: It's not right.
sentences.zh: 这太不对了。

sentences.en: I've got police protection outside my house.
sentences.zh: 我的房子外面有警察在保护。

sentences.en: Fine.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You know, I took a higher-profile job.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我接了一份更高调的工作。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我懂。

sentences.en: Secretary ran for office.
sentences.zh: 秘书竞选了公职。

sentences.en: His wife knew that, too.
sentences.zh: 他妻子也知道这一点。

sentences.en: This kid took a job.
sentences.zh: 这个年轻人接了一份工作。

sentences.en: He just took a job.
sentences.zh: 他只是接了一份工作。

sentences.en: And it's just wrong.
sentences.zh: 而这完全是错的。

sentences.en: I can't begin to explain the level of anger I have right now over this.
sentences.zh: 我简直无法形容我对此感到的愤怒程度。

sentences.en: And every American, every Georgian, Republican and Democrat alike should have that same level of anger.
sentences.zh: 而且每一个美国人，每一个佐治亚州人，无论是共和党人还是民主党人，都应该有同样程度的愤怒。

sentences.en: Mr. President, it looks like you likely lost the state of Georgia.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，看起来你很可能输掉了佐治亚州。

sentences.en: We're investigating.
sentences.zh: 我们在调查。

sentences.en: There's always a possibility.
sentences.zh: 一直都有这种可能。

sentences.en: I get it.
sentences.zh: 我懂。

sentences.en: And you have the rights to go through the courts.
sentences.zh: 你们有通过法庭解决的权利。

sentences.en: What you don't have the ability to do, and you need to step up and say this, is stop inspiring people to commit potential acts of violence.
sentences.zh: 你们没有能力做、而且需要站出来表态的是，停止煽动人们去实施潜在的暴力行为。

sentences.en: Someone's going to get hurt.
sentences.zh: 会有人受伤的。

sentences.en: Someone's going to get shot.
sentences.zh: 会有人中枪的。

sentences.en: Someone's going to get killed.
sentences.zh: 会有人丧命的。

sentences.en: And it's not right.
sentences.zh: 这太不对了。

sentences.en: I, I, it's not right.
sentences.zh: 我，我，这太不对了。

sentences.en: And y'all, I don't have anything scripted.
sentences.zh: 而且各位，我没有准备任何稿子。

sentences.en: This is, like I said, I'm going to do my best to keep it together.
sentences.zh: 就像我说的，我会尽力控制住自己的情绪。

sentences.en: Mr. President, as the Secretary said yesterday, people aren't giving you the best advice on what's actually going on the ground.
sentences.zh: 总统先生，正如秘书昨天所说，对于实地实际发生的情况，人们并没有给你最好的建议。

sentences.en: It's time to look forward.
sentences.zh: 是时候向前看了。

sentences.en: If you want to run for your election in four years, fine.
sentences.zh: 如果你想在四年后竞选，随便你。

sentences.en: Do it.
sentences.zh: 去吧。

sentences.en: But everything we're seeing right now, there's not a path.
sentences.zh: 但从我们目前看到的一切来看，这条路行不通。

sentences.en: Be the bigger man here.
sentences.zh: 拿出点气度来吧。

sentences.en: And stop, step in.
sentences.zh: 停下来，介入吧。

sentences.en: Tell your supporters, don't be violent.
sentences.zh: 告诉你的支持者，不要使用暴力。

sentences.en: Don't intimidate.
sentences.zh: 不要恐吓。

sentences.en: All that's wrong.
sentences.zh: 这些全都是错的。

sentences.en: It's un-American.
sentences.zh: 这有悖于美国精神。

sentences.en: I don't know what else to say on that front.
sentences.zh: 在这方面我不知道还能说些什么。

sentences.en: I mean, these are elections.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是选举。

sentences.en: One of our goals was to make elections boring again.
sentences.zh: 我们的目标之一就是让选举重新变得枯燥乏味。

sentences.en: Well, guess what?
sentences.zh: 结果呢？

sentences.en: That didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: This is all.
sentences.zh: 就这些。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Are you nervous?
sentences.zh: 你紧张吗？

sentences.en: As you delivered all this, did you understand that it was going to be a very big deal?
sentences.zh: 当你发表所有这些言论时，你明白这会成为一件大事吗？

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，没有。

sentences.en: No way in God's green acre did I think it was going to be a big deal.
sentences.zh: 上帝在上，我绝对没想过这会是一件大事。

sentences.en: I thought it would be a quick thing here in local stuff, but I was pissed off.
sentences.zh: 我以为这只是本地的一件小快事，但我当时气极了。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Dude, there's no—nobody walks up thinking, hey, this is going to make national, international happen.
sentences.zh: 老兄，没有人会觉得——没有人会走出来想，嘿，这会引起全国乃至国际的关注。

sentences.en: Nobody thinks that.
sentences.zh: 没有人会这么想。

sentences.en: That's not a normal response.
sentences.zh: 这不是正常的反应。

sentences.en: I mean, and in fact, it was really funny that day, my fiancé had gotten a new job, and I found out about three hours before this happened.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，事实上，那天挺搞笑的，我未婚妻刚找到一份新工作，我在这事发生前大约三小时才得知。

sentences.en: And I promised her, I said, we're going to focus on you.
sentences.zh: 我答应过她，我说，我们要把重心放在你身上。

sentences.en: We're going to go to dinner.
sentences.zh: 我们要去吃晚饭。

sentences.en: We're going to have a great night.
sentences.zh: 我们要过个美好的夜晚。

sentences.en: And so I had to go do it.
sentences.zh: 所以我必须去处理这事。

sentences.en: Tonight, today is about you.
sentences.zh: 今晚，今天是属于你的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, my phone was blowing up, but I figured it was local.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我的手机一直在响个不停，但我以为只是本地的事。

sentences.en: I didn't really worry about it.
sentences.zh: 我并没有太担心。

sentences.en: And then we went to dinner, and I told her I was not going to look at my phone.
sentences.zh: 然后我们去吃晚饭了，我告诉她我不会看手机。

sentences.en: And we got home at like 11, and my phone was still blowing up.
sentences.zh: 我们大概11点回到家，我的手机依然在狂响。

sentences.en: And I go to—I'm getting ready to go to bed, and I just, you know, hit Twitter and stuff before I go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我准备去——我正准备睡觉，睡觉前我只是，你知道的，刷了一下推特什么的。

sentences.en: I'm like, huh, this is getting a little more pick-up-and-play than I thought or intended.
sentences.zh: 我在想，哈，这比我想象或预期的要受关注得多了。

sentences.en: So, yeah, it was—at this point, it's still otherworldly to me.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，当时情况是——对现在的我来说，它仍然很不真实。

sentences.en: It still doesn't feel real.
sentences.zh: 它依然感觉不像是真的。

sentences.en: It's just—like I said, the New York Times podcast would not normally be talking to somebody with the title Voting System Implementation Manager.
sentences.zh: 这只是——就像我说的，《纽约时报》的播客平时不会去采访一个头衔是“投票系统实施经理”的人。

sentences.en: That's not normal.
sentences.zh: 这很不正常。

sentences.en: Fair.
sentences.zh: 也是。

sentences.en: So—
sentences.zh: 所以——

sentences.en: But it was such a break from how Republicans had been handling the moment to date.
sentences.zh: 但这与共和党人迄今为止处理这一时刻的方式截然不同。

sentences.en: That's why I asked you if you understood that it might be a big deal.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我问你是否明白这可能是一件大事。

sentences.en: So that's why I am not surprised that it got the response that it did.
sentences.zh: 所以我对它引发这种反响并不感到意外。

sentences.en: Well, in retrospect now, with people across the country, I mean, it's good and bad.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在回想起来，全国各地的人们的反应，怎么说呢，有好的也有坏的。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm getting a lot of support, a lot of emails.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我得到了很多支持，收到了很多电子邮件。

sentences.en: You know, flowers got sent to me yesterday.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，昨天还给我寄了花。

sentences.en: That was new.
sentences.zh: 这还是头一次。

sentences.en: Who sent you flowers?
sentences.zh: 谁给你送的花？

sentences.en: Some random person from Connecticut saying thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 康涅狄格州的一个陌生人，说非常感谢。

sentences.en: I just got another handwritten note from—let's see, somebody in Macon, Georgia.
sentences.zh: 我刚刚又收到了一封手写便条，让我看看——来自佐治亚州梅肯市的某个人。

sentences.en: Another handwritten thank you note from something in Bellingham, Washington.
sentences.zh: 还有一封来自华盛顿州贝灵厄姆某人的手写感谢信。

sentences.en: Could you just read a line or two from one of those?
sentences.zh: 你能读一读其中一封信的一两行吗？

sentences.en: Thank you for being so strong and assuring the results of our elections are honeSt.
sentences.zh: 感谢你如此坚定并确保我们选举结果的诚实。

sentences.en: You've done a great job of not allowing our president and the other bullies to get you to say or do things that are not true.
sentences.zh: 你做得很好，没有让我们的总统和其他霸凌者迫使你说出或做出不真实的事情。

sentences.en: Keep staying strong.
sentences.zh: 请继续保持坚强。

sentences.en: Let's see.
sentences.zh: 我看看。

sentences.en: Thank you for your leadership.
sentences.zh: 感谢你的领导力。

sentences.en: During this difficult time, you've been a shining star.
sentences.zh: 在这个艰难的时刻，你一直是一颗闪亮的明星。

sentences.en: At great personal cost, you stood solidly for integrity, the truth, and doing the right thing.
sentences.zh: 你付出了巨大的个人代价，坚定不移地捍卫诚信、真相和做正确的事。

sentences.en: It is individuals like you that give us hope for the future.
sentences.zh: 正是像你这样的人给了我们对未来的希望。

sentences.en: Yes, those are wonderful things to get.
sentences.zh: 是的，收到这些真是太美好了。

sentences.en: But if I ever want to get my ego put back in place, I can go to my email where I can go back to my death threats.
sentences.zh: 但如果我想让我的自我认知回到现实，我可以去看看我的电子邮件，那里有我的死亡威胁。

sentences.en: So those are things that can keep things even-keeled.
sentences.zh: 所以这些东西能让人保持平衡的心态。

sentences.en: So this is a real mixed bag.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一场真正的喜忧参半。

sentences.en: It's a mixed bag.
sentences.zh: 真是五味杂陈。

sentences.en: I wonder how you felt and feel about becoming essentially in an instant.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，对于转瞬间几乎变得——你是怎么看待和感受这一切的。

sentences.en: I mean, I have to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我得坦白。

sentences.en: I had never heard of you before I saw you in a video online.
sentences.zh: 在网上看到你的视频之前，我从来没听说过你。

sentences.en: You're not supposed to have heard of me.
sentences.zh: 你本来就不应该听说过我。

sentences.en: I was a city councilman in a random city.
sentences.zh: 我只是一个普通城市的市议会议员。

sentences.en: There's a voting system implementation manager.
sentences.zh: 我只是个投票系统实施经理。

sentences.en: There's no reason normally for you to have ever heard of me.
sentences.zh: 正常情况下，你根本没有理由听说过我。

sentences.en: But I wonder how you feel because in, as I said, just an instant, you become a pretty singular figure within your party, the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 但我想知道你的感受，因为正如我所说，就在转瞬间，你成了你所在的政党——共和党内一个非常独特的人物。

sentences.en: Someone who came out at a moment when the entire Republican Party, more or less,
sentences.zh: 当整个共和党差不多都

sentences.en: was still defending the president or staying silent and doing the opposite and calling out the president, leaders of the party, saying something is very, very wrong here.
sentences.zh: 还在为总统辩护或保持沉默、做着相反的事并怒斥总统和党内领袖——说这里面有非常非常严重的问题时，你却在这样一个时刻挺身而出。

sentences.en: How did it feel to become that person?
sentences.zh: 成为这样一个人是什么感觉？

sentences.en: Let's be honest, Michael, until you just said that.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，说实话，直到你刚才这么说之前。

sentences.en: I hadn't considered myself that person.
sentences.zh: 我都没把自己当成那样的人。

sentences.en: I mean, I've been doing a lot of interviews.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我一直在接受很多采访。

sentences.en: I get that.
sentences.zh: 我明白。

sentences.en: But I just – I'm a process guy.
sentences.zh: 但我只是——我是一个注重流程的人。

sentences.en: I am a – my first Republican campaign, I was 15 years old.
sentences.zh: 我是一个——我参加第一次共和党竞选时才15岁。

sentences.en: I've been in this party for essentially it defines a large part of what my life is like.
sentences.zh: 我加入这个党基本上已经定义了我生活中的很大一部分。

sentences.en: And I've now been forced to – you're not the first person to suggest something like that,
sentences.zh: 而我现在被迫——你不是第一个暗示这种事的人，

sentences.en: but you put it in a succinct way that had not – I had not looked at it at that angle necessarily.
sentences.zh: 但你用一种简明扼要的方式表达了出来，而我以前并没有——我没有从那个角度去看待它。

sentences.en: The party has values and things I care about, and I'm going to continue to fight for the sanity and the sanctity of that party to carry those positions.
sentences.zh: 这个党有我所珍视的价值观和事物，我将继续为这个党的理智与神圣性而战，以承载这些立场。

sentences.en: Now, an underlying attachment to that is a dedication to Republican as in the institutions of the republic set of values.
sentences.zh: 现在，其中隐含的一种附属关系是对共和党人身份的奉献，这里的共和国指的是共和国的各种制度和价值观。

sentences.en: You know, a judiciary that is believed, a free press that is protected, an election and system that is done with integrity in such a way that no matter who wins and who loses,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，一个受到信任的司法系统，一个得到保护的自由媒体，一个以诚信方式进行的选举和系统，无论谁输谁赢，

sentences.en: both sides say, yes, we lost, we won.
sentences.zh: 双方都会说，是的，我们输了，我们赢了。

sentences.en: We'll move on to fight another day, an ability for government to function because the only way capitalism, our neighborhoods – this is something I've been saying.
sentences.zh: 我们继续前进，改天再战，政府具备正常运转的能力，因为资本主义和我们的社区唯有如此——这也是我一直在说的一点。

sentences.en: I think that everybody who gets any higher elected office has to have served at least one term on a city council, school board,
sentences.zh: 我认为每一个赢得更高公职的人都必须在市议会、学校董事会

sentences.en: or county commission because that's where real work gets done.
sentences.zh: 或县委员会至少担任过一届任期，因为真正的实干都是在那里完成的。

sentences.en: It's not just giving speeches.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是发表长篇大论。

sentences.en: You have to actually find ways to make things work.
sentences.zh: 你必须真正找到让事情运转起来的方法。

sentences.en: And I'm a believer that roads are supposed to be paved.
sentences.zh: 我相信道路本来就该是铺好的。

sentences.en: You're not supposed to think about it.
sentences.zh: 你根本不应该去操心它。

sentences.en: When you call the police, they're supposed to show up.
sentences.zh: 当你报警时，警察就应该出现。

sentences.en: You're not supposed to think about it.
sentences.zh: 你根本不应该去操心它。

sentences.en: Your military is supposed to be, you know, well-stocked and put in the right places.
sentences.zh: 你们的军队应该，你知道的，装备精良并部署在正确的位置。

sentences.en: You're supposed to follow your treaties.
sentences.zh: 你们应该遵守条约。

sentences.en: I mean, there's norms and things we all have to uphold for the entire system to work.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，为了让整个系统正常运转，我们都必须维护各种规范和事物。

sentences.en: And if those things fall apart or are attacked by either side, I mean, it hurts everybody in the long run.
sentences.zh: 如果这些东西崩溃了，或者受到任何一方的攻击，从长远来看，这会伤害到所有人。

sentences.en: And one of the things that bothers me, and this is about Republicans and Democrats alike, especially in D.C.,
sentences.zh: 让我困扰的事情之一，无论是共和党人还是民主党人，尤其是在华盛顿特区，

sentences.en: undermining the left from the left, undermining the right from the right,
sentences.zh: 左翼从内部瓦解左翼，右翼从内部瓦解右翼，

sentences.en: and making everybody else the other and the enemy as opposed to somebody who I have philosophical opposition to,
sentences.zh: 把所有其他人推向对立面并视作敌人，而不是仅仅持不同政见的人，

sentences.en: I don't think most elected officials on either side want to see the other side burn in a fire.
sentences.zh: 我不认为双方的大多数民选官员都希望看到对方在烈火中毁灭。

sentences.en: But both sides essentially say, hey, the other side wins.
sentences.zh: 但双方基本上都在说，嘿，如果对方赢了，

sentences.en: You're going to burn in a fire.
sentences.zh: 你就会在烈火中毁灭。

sentences.en: That is because they've now moved to base level politics because that's in vogue today.
sentences.zh: 那是因为他们现在已经沦为底层政治，因为这在今天是时髦的。

sentences.en: And maybe there's a way you can get back to sanity.
sentences.zh: 或许有一种方法能让你们重回理智。

sentences.en: I mean, and there's people on my part say that's being a squish.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我党内有人说这是软弱的表现。

sentences.en: There's people on the other side going, well, you need to be a hard left to be really true to the socialist agenda we have.
sentences.zh: 另一边的人则说，好吧，为了真正忠于我们的社会主义议程，你需要变得极左。

sentences.en: I mean, there's both sides to do this.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，双方都这么做。

sentences.en: And maybe my way of doing things is out of vogue.
sentences.zh: 也许我做事的方式已经过时了。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: But that's the way I've always viewed it.
sentences.zh: 但这一直是我看待事物的方式。

sentences.en: Well, you're sort of getting at what I was curious about, whether you were conflicted at all about this role that you have now taken on,
sentences.zh: 嗯，你其实触及了我很好奇的一点，那就是你对于自己现在承担的这个角色是否曾有过任何内心冲突，

sentences.en: given your status as a lifelong Republican, a proud Republican, to be seen by some of your fellow Republicans and maybe even its current leader as a kind of traitor, a betrayer.
sentences.zh: 鉴于你作为一个终身共和党人、一个引以为豪的共和党人的身份，却被你的一些同僚甚至可能是现任党魁视为某种叛徒、背叛者。

sentences.en: But it seems like you're saying actually you see what you are doing here as your duty to the Republican Party.
sentences.zh: 但听起来你似乎认为，实际上你所做的一切正是你对共和党应尽的职责。

sentences.en: And I'm telling you, this kid, I haven't talked to him yet, and I want to.
sentences.zh: 我跟你说，这孩子，我还没跟他谈过，但我很想谈谈。

sentences.en: Had it not been for that, I don't know if I would have had that moment.
sentences.zh: 要不是那样，我不知道我当时会不会有那种感觉。

sentences.en: And, excuse me a second, it was a real, it was tough.
sentences.zh: 而且，失陪一下，这真的很不容易，非常艰难。

sentences.en: You're real emotional about it, aren't you?
sentences.zh: 你对此感触很深，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I don't want to do that in public, but okay.
sentences.zh: 我本不想在公众面前这样，但好吧。

sentences.en: So this is about the future of a nation that I've spent a lot of my time trying to make better
sentences.zh: 所以这是关于一个国家的未来，我花了很多时间试图让它变得更好

sentences.en: at the national level, local level, state level.
sentences.zh: 在国家层面、地方层面、州层面。

sentences.en: And I was never supposed to be this.
sentences.zh: 我从来没想过会变成这样。

sentences.en: I'm, people have heard it before, if you've read some of the things,
sentences.zh: 我是说，大家以前都听过，如果你读过一些报道的话，

sentences.en: I'm the detail-oriented, nuts and bolts, let's make it work guy.
sentences.zh: 我是一个注重细节、关注核心、脚踏实地把事情做好的人。

sentences.en: That's what I do.
sentences.zh: 这就是我做的事。

sentences.en: So how does the actions of the leader of the party, the president of the United States, the top Republican in the country, and his supporters responding to him,
sentences.zh: 那么，党内领导人、美国总统、全国顶级共和党人的所作所为，以及他的支持者对他的反应，

sentences.en: and the fact that only a few Republicans are speaking out against it, how is that leaving you feeling about the Republican Party at this moment, about so many of your colleagues?
sentences.zh: 再加上只有少数共和党人站出来反对这一切，这一切让你对当下的共和党作何感想？对你的那么多同事作何感想？

sentences.en: Did they talk to you?
sentences.zh: 他们跟你谈过吗？

sentences.en: What did they say about what you had said to them?
sentences.zh: 他们对你对他们说的话有什么反应？

sentences.en: Because you had basically said to them, you're being kind of cowardly.
sentences.zh: 因为你基本上对他们说过，你们有点像懦夫。

sentences.en: I guess to a degree, I did do that.
sentences.zh: 我想某种程度上，我确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And I, again, I wasn't thinking, I was just going.
sentences.zh: 而且我，再说一次，我当时没多想，只是顺着说下去了。

sentences.en: So mostly I've gotten positive feedback from most of them saying, man, somebody should send us sooner, wish we could do that.
sentences.zh: 所以大多数人给我的反馈都是积极的，他们说，天哪，早就该有人这么说了，真希望我们也能做到。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of them say-
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们很多人说——

sentences.en: Wait, they say they wish they could do that, but of course they can do that.
sentences.zh: 等等，他们说希望自己能做到，但他们当然可以做到啊。

sentences.en: They could, but they said, we don't recognize our party anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们可以，但他们说，我们已经认不出我们的党了。

sentences.en: Maybe over time we can do it.
sentences.zh: 也许随着时间的推移，我们能做到吧。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I wonder if you thought that this speech you gave was going to change anything.
sentences.zh: 我在想，你是否认为你发表的这番演讲会改变什么。

sentences.en: And I don't mean to sound overly cynical, but I would have been surprised if it did.
sentences.zh: 我不是故意显得过于冷嘲热讽，但如果真的改变了，我才会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: And in the time since, the president has not stopped questioning legitimacy election.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，总统一直没有停止质疑选举的合法性。

sentences.en: In fact, he has since then delivered a speech in which he repeated these baseless claims about fraud from the White House.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他自那以后发表了一次演讲，在白宫再次重复了这些毫无根据的舞弊指控。

sentences.en: His lawyers, as you know, they're in Georgia making similar claiMs.
sentences.zh: 如你所知，他的律师们正在佐治亚州提出类似的指控。

sentences.en: They're making those claims online.
sentences.zh: 他们正在网上提出这些指控。

sentences.en: They're posting conspiratorial videos about suitcases and ballots in Georgia.
sentences.zh: 他们发布了关于佐治亚州行李箱和选票的阴谋论视频。

sentences.en: And we're speaking to you, of course, on Friday.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们是在周五采访你的。

sentences.en: Tomorrow, the president himself will be in Georgia delivering a speech that we expect will be more of the same.
sentences.zh: 明天，总统本人将前往佐治亚州发表演讲，我们预计那将是老调重弹。

sentences.en: And as you say, Republicans may be telling you privately they wish that they could say something, but they aren't saying anything.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，共和党人私下里可能会告诉你，他们希望自己能说点什么，但他们什么也没说。

sentences.en: So it doesn't feel like this speech had its intended effect.
sentences.zh: 所以感觉这番演讲并没有达到预期的效果。

sentences.en: It did to a degree.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上达到了。

sentences.en: They at least got out there and said, yes, of course, we condemn violence.
sentences.zh: 他们至少站出来说，是的，当然，我们谴责暴力。

sentences.en: That's at least one thing.
sentences.zh: 这至少是一点。

sentences.en: And I've got more of my local elected state folks here believing what we're telling them.
sentences.zh: 我这里有更多当选的州地方官员相信我们所说的话。

sentences.en: So, but I will say this.
sentences.zh: 所以，但我还是要说：

sentences.en: It shouldn't be a big deal for people to say what they think in a way with integrity and have that suddenly be, wow, that's really strange and novel.
sentences.zh: 人们以正直的方式说出自己的想法，这本不该是什么大事，不该突然让人觉得“哇，这真的好奇怪、好新鲜”。

sentences.en: It shouldn't be that hard.
sentences.zh: 这不该这么难。

sentences.en: But that is in some ways the story of the Trump era in the Republican Party, your party.
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，这就是特朗普时代在共和党、在你们党内的写照。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I just want to clarify one thing.
sentences.zh: 我只想澄清一件事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Who most of all do you hope heard you giving that speech?
sentences.zh: 你最希望听到你发表那番演讲的是谁？

sentences.en: Who would you like to imagine listening to it?
sentences.zh: 你希望想象谁在听？

sentences.en: And what would you like for it to have meant to them?
sentences.zh: 你希望这对他们意味着什么？

sentences.en: Honestly, there's hundreds of thousands of election workers around the country who pulled off this election.
sentences.zh: 老实说，全国有成千上万名选举工作人员，是他们完成了这场选举。

sentences.en: They need to know somebody's on their side and in their corner.
sentences.zh: 他们需要知道有人站在他们这边，支持他们。

sentences.en: That's who I most wanted to hear.
sentences.zh: 这就是我最想让他们听到的人。

sentences.en: And especially I wanted that kid and his family to hear it.
sentences.zh: 我尤其希望那个孩子和他的家人听到。

sentences.en: He needed to hear that.
sentences.zh: 他需要听到这些。

sentences.en: Mr. Sterling, we really want to thank you for your time and for your work.
sentences.zh: 斯特林先生，我们非常感谢您抽出时间并感谢您的工作。

sentences.en: And we appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们对此深表感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: You have a great day.
sentences.zh: 祝你过愉快的一天。

sentences.zh: 在周六晚上佐治亚州的集会之前，特朗普总统致电该州州长

sentences.en: It does not appear that Kemp will do that.
sentences.zh: 坎普似乎不会这么做。

sentences.zh: 我不得不说，几个小时后。

sentences.zh: 我会去佛罗里达州，轻松自在地生活，到处走走，然后说我干得不错。

sentences.zh: 但你绝不能接受他们偷窃、操纵和抢劫。

sentences.zh: 绝不能接受。

sentences.zh: 在他的集会期间。

sentences.zh: 你知道，我们赢了佐治亚州，只要你们明白这一点。
